the marines' first meal after cryosleep

Flour tortillas stuffed with chorizo, soft scrambled eggs, crispy potato, cheddar and salsa, rolled tight and toasted in a hot pan until golden. Dice 400g potatoes and fry in oil for 12 minutes until crisp. Slice 2 chorizo sausages and fry until the fat runs. Whisk 8 eggs with salt and scramble softly in 20g butter. Lay out 4 large flour tortillas and fill each with potato, chorizo, egg, 30g grated cheddar and 2 tbsp salsa. Fold in the sides, roll tight and toast seam side down in a dry pan for 2 minutes a side.
W: Vanilla panna cotta set in a round mould, turned out, with candied orange peel strips as legs fanned around it.
K: strong enough to get you out of cryosleep

Strong cold brew poured over ice and sweet condensed milk in tall glasses, stirred until creamy, with a pinch of cinnamon on top. The night before, stir 100g coarsely ground dark roast coffee into 800ml cold water, cover and refrigerate 12 to 16 hours, then strain through a paper filter. Spoon 2 tbsp sweetened condensed milk into each of 4 tall glasses. Fill with ice, pour 180ml cold brew into each and stir until creamy. Dust with a pinch of cinnamon.

edition.cue: Serve the snacks at the marines' breakfast on the Sulaco.

s.note: Golden buttermilk cornbread baked in a hot buttered pan.
s.how: Heat the oven to 200°C conventional with a 20cm ovenproof skillet inside. Mix 100g fine cornmeal, 80g plain flour, 20g caster sugar, 1 tsp baking powder and 1/4 tsp salt. Whisk 150ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 30g melted butter, then stir into the dry ingredients. Carefully butter the hot skillet with 10g butter, pour in the batter and bake for 20 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes and cut into 8 squares.

s.note: Long crisp dough sticks brushed with oil, sesame and salt.
s.how: Roll 250g pizza dough into 12 long thin sticks. Place on a lined tray, brush with 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil and roll in 15g sesame seeds and 1/2 tsp sea salt flakes. Bake at 220°C conventional for 12 minutes until crisp and golden. Cool slightly before serving.

m.note: Beef and pork loaf with tomato glaze and creamy mashed potato.
m.how: Soak 50g breadcrumbs in 80ml milk for 5 minutes. Mix with 350g beef mince, 250g pork mince, 1 egg, 1 finely diced onion, 1 tbsp anchovy-free Worcestershire sauce, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Shape into a loaf on a lined tray and glaze with 60g tomato sauce. Bake at 180°C conventional for 1 hour until cooked through, at least 75°C in the centre. Rest 10 minutes. Meanwhile peel and chop 800g potatoes, boil 20 minutes until tender and mash with 40g butter and 100ml warm milk. Slice the loaf and serve with mash.

w.note: Wobbly vanilla cream with candied orange peel strips fanned around it.
w.how: Soak 4g gelatine leaves, using the packet's equivalent weight, in cold water for 5 minutes. Warm 250ml thickened cream, 150ml full cream milk, 40g caster sugar and seeds of half a vanilla bean over low heat until steaming, without boiling. Remove from heat, squeeze the gelatine dry and stir in until dissolved. Divide into four lightly oiled 100ml round moulds and refrigerate at least 4 hours until set. Dip each mould briefly in warm water and turn out. Fan 40g candied orange peel strips around the puddings as legs.
